title: PNG file structure
summary: A PNG file starts with an 8-byte signature, then a sequence of chunks. Each chunk: 4-byte length (big-endian), 4-byte type (ASCII), length bytes of data, 4-byte CRC-32 (over type+data). Critical chunks: IHDR (image header), PLTE (palette), IDAT (image data), IEND (end). Ancillary chunks: tEXt/zTXt/iTXt (metadata), gAMA, cHRM, sRGB, pHYs, tIME, bKGD, etc.

structure.meaning: Length of the chunk data field (big-endian). Max 2^31-1.
The chunk's payload (structure depends on type).
CRC-32 (IEEE) over chunk type + chunk data.
Width (4), Height (4), Bit depth (1), Color type (1), Compression (1, always 0), Filter (1, always 0), Interlace (1, 0/1).

ext.example_decoded: PNG signature + IHDR for a 1x1 8-bit RGB image
notes: Signature bytes: 0x89 (high bit set, catches 7-bit stripping), 'PNG', CRLF (line-ending detection), 0x1A (stops display), LF.
Critical chunks must appear in order: IHDR first, then PLTE (if color type 3), then IDAT(s), then IEND last.
Ancillary chunks can appear anywhere between IHDR and IEND.
Color types: 0 grayscale, 2 RGB, 3 indexed, 4 grayscale+alpha, 6 RGBA.
IDAT contains zlib-compressed (DEFLATE) scanlines, each prefixed by a filter byte (0-4).
